tasks.instruction: Write a discussion response. An effective response contains at least 100 words.

professor.name: Doctor Achebe
professor.text: In the next few weeks, we'll be talking about urban traffic management. Let's begin by discussing one popular idea—creating car-free central zones. Some cities around the world have recently designated their downtown areas as being automobile-free, which means that vehicles are not allowed to enter the city centers. Do you think that more cities should make their central zones car-free? Why or why not?

posts.name: Claire
posts.text: I support the idea of establishing car-free central zones because this will result in one important benefit for city residents—it will be better for their health. Instead of driving everywhere. People will be encouraged to walk or cycle more. It would be a great way to incorporate exercise into people's routines.

posts.name: Paul
posts.text: It sounds like a good idea, but I'm skeptical. My main concern is that many businesses located in the city centers, such as shops and restaurants, may suffer because customers will no longer be able to reach those businesses by car. For some customers, if they can't drive, they won't go at all.

tasks.sample:
In my opinion, it is not a good idea to ban vehicles in downtown areas.

First of all, it creates inconveniences for citizens. In many cities, most crucial facilities such as schools and hospitals, especially the best ones, are located in downtown areas. If vehicles are completely banned in these areas, it would be difficult for citizens to access these facilities. For example, if people living in the city center are severely sick or injured, they would have to walk to the hospital because ambulances are not allowed there, which is ridiculous to imagine.

Moreover, the overall economy would be crippled by the car-free policy because the car industry would be significantly impacted. If governments forbid driving in the downtown area, customers would be discouraged from buying cars, leading to a decrease in car sales. Car manufacturers would, in turn, limit their production and even start laying off their employees, causing numerous engineers, streamlined workers, salespeople, and even people in the advertising industry to lose their jobs.

Therefore, a car-free policy has a negative influence on the whole society.
